Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The MOSIP-based e-ID system includes digital authentication functionality. The IDEMIA/Atos solution includes a 'citizen portal, mobile app, contact center, private cloud, cybersecurity, core biometric system.' ANID shared with Senegal how it 'integrated MOSIP to facilitate access to services.' MOSIP inherently supports digital authentication including online/offline biometric verification.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Togo operates a government services portal (servicespublics.gouv.tg) that had 526 daily connections by June 2022 and over 40,000 passport applications processed. The IDEMIA/Atos citizen portal is designed to authenticate users for government services. The NIU is designed as 'a single access key to various public services.' Government portal authentication via the e-ID is part of the system design.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No credible evidence found of a functioning individual data access/self-service portal where citizens can view their own registered data. The ANID system and MOSIP platform support such features technically, but no public announcement or active portal for individual data viewing has been documented in Togo's deployment as of 2025. Searched ANID website, Togo First, CIPESA, and interweave.africa.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Togo has used its biometric voter ID database for electronic KYC (e-KYC) in the Novissi social protection program, demonstrating KYC enablement in practice. The national ID card issued by DGDN is the primary KYC document per Smile ID. The new e-ID/NIU is explicitly designed to 'reduce fraud in the financial sector' and enable KYC for banks and telecom operators.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Togo's general legal framework (cybersecurity law 2018, data protection law 2019) provides judicial recourse for data rights violations. CIPESA notes courts have ruled on digital rights cases in Togo. However, there is no specific ID-dedicated judicial oversight mechanism; oversight is through general courts and the IPDCP administrative authority.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Law No. 2020-009 (Arts. 10, 21, 22) requires ANID to encode/encrypt data and limits access to authorised agents. Law No. 2019-014 sets data sharing principles. However, Law No. 2012-018 (Art. 92) allows interception by multiple ministers. Rules are partially codified but contain gaps and inconsistent application, making this 'partially' available.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Law No. 2020-009 of September 10, 2020 is specifically on biometric identification of natural persons in Togo (e-ID Togo), amended in 2022 by Law No. 2022-010. This law is dedicated to digital ID, establishing ANID and the NIU system, making it a digital-ID-specific regulation.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Togo enacted Law No. 2019-014 of October 29, 2019 relating to the protection of personal data. This is a comprehensive data protection act. The law established the IPDCP (Instance de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel) via decree of December 9, 2020.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The IPDCP (Instance de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel) was established by decree on December 9, 2020, as an independent administrative authority overseeing personal data processing by public and private entities. By March 2025 the IPDCP launched its public activities and signed a memorandum of cooperation with the HAAC (December 2025).

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Under Law No. 2020-009, the NIU (Unique Identification Number) constitutes legal proof of identity for interactions with public administration. The ANID head stated 'the NIU is proof of identity.' The law mandates that NIUs be included in all administrative documents issued to citizens.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Togo has a dedicated legal framework: Law No. 2020-009 of September 10, 2020 on biometric identification of natural persons, amended by Law No. 2022-010 of June 24, 2022. Additionally, Law No. 2019-014 of October 29, 2019 on personal data protection and the December 2020 decree establishing the IPDCP provide the governance framework.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The IDEMIA/Atos contract includes a knowledge and skills transfer program, with Atos establishing a subsidiary in Togo for long-term sustainability and local capacity building. However, the core system was designed, built and is run by the foreign consortium (IDEMIA and Atos), making this partial in-country maintenance. Domestic capacity is being built but foreign vendors still dominate operations.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The e-ID project is managed by ANID under the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Transformation, not directly the Ministry of Finance. However, the Finance/Budget Minister oversees government financial commitments and participated in related reforms (e.g., AML law Dec 2025). The World Bank WURI project financial oversight is through the planning ministry. Finance ministry has partial but not full oversight of the digital ID programme.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The IDEMIA/Atos e-ID solution collects 10 fingerprints, facial photograph, and 2 iris scans (facial/iris). The ANID law (Art.4, Law 2020-009) specifies photograph/facial recognition, fingerprints, and iris scan. This exceeds fingerprints-only and qualifies as Facial/Iris category.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The e-ID system uses MOSIP, a cloud-based digital platform hosted on a private cloud built by IDEMIA/Atos. ANID stores biometric and biographical data in an encrypted digital central database. The system is fully digital (not paper or hybrid).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The national ID card (and voter ID) are accepted but not mandatory for banking/KYC in Togo. Smile ID notes the national ID card is the 'primary KYC document.' Multiple ID types (national ID, voter ID, passport, driver's license) are accepted. The new e-ID/NIU is designed to enable financial inclusion and reduce fraud in finance, but is not yet mandatory for banking.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The e-ID Togo / NIU issuance is explicitly free of charge. The ANID website and project documentation state it is a 'free, inclusive national identification system.' The World Bank WURI financing covers enrollment costs. (Note: the older traditional national ID card cost XOF 5,000, but the new e-ID/NIU enrollment is free per official documentation.)

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Under the amended Law No. 2022-010 and ANID guidelines, all residents including children from birth (age 0) are eligible. Children aged 0-4 have only biographical data collected (no biometrics). The ANID website confirms 'All citizens are eligible for the e-ID Togo project, including children aged zero to five, who can be registered using a parent's NIU.' This corresponds to eligibility from birth (<1 year).

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Article 13 of Law No. 2020-009 states biometric registration is not an obligation for individual citizens (technically optional). However, the law also states the NIU will be required for all administrative interactions, school exams, and government services - effectively making it mandatory for some services and social participation. This is 'mandatory for some' contexts.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The NIU is designed to enable access to universal health insurance and health services. The ANID page states the e-ID will 'guarantee health coverage and access to basic services.' However, as the e-ID rollout is still in progress, full mandatory use for healthcare has not been confirmed. The system is designed for healthcare access (accepted), not yet mandatorily enforced.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Law No. 2020-009 mandates that all persons residing in Togo—'without distinction of race, gender, religion or nationality'—obtain a NIU. The ANID website describes e-ID Togo as available to 'each Togolese citizen and foreign resident.' All non-nationals residing in Togo are eligible.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No specific documented independent security review or penetration test of the Togo e-ID system was found. The MOSIP platform has built-in security features and cybersecurity is part of the IDEMIA/Atos contract. The Agence Nationale de Cybersécurité (ANCy) exists in Togo, but no evidence of a published independent security audit of the e-ID system specifically was found. Searched ANID, BiometricUpdate, CIPESA, World Bank documentation.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: During Novissi COVID cash transfers, voter ID (biometric) was required/accepted but the program was not fully mandatory for all social services. The NIU is explicitly designed as access key to social services, pensions, and social protection programs, and the World Bank WURI document notes the e-ID will be the gateway to benefits. Currently accepted but not yet universally mandatory.
